title: Tech Note: New Entry Points in 4th Dimension 3.5.3
author: ACI and ACI US Engineering
featured_technology: 4D external package / plugin API (Ext4D.h entry points)

historical_commentary.text: This is a low-level plugin/external-package developer reference documenting three new C-level entry points added in 4th Dimension 3.5.3: bulk-copying a selection's field values into arrays, installing custom Sequential Operation/Printing progress hooks from within a plugin, and introspecting other installed external packages. These entry points are part of 4D's original 68K/PowerPC/Windows external package API (Ext4D.h), which predates the modern 4D Plugin SDK by many major architecture generations; the specific struct layouts, parameter block conventions, and platform-detection patterns shown are obsolete, though the general need (bulk data extraction to arrays, custom progress UI, and inter-plugin communication) persists conceptually in the modern plugin architecture.
related_updates: 4D's plugin/external package architecture has been substantially rearchitected since 1996 (multiple generations predating the modern 4D Plugin SDK), so these specific low-level entry points and ParameterBlock conventions no longer apply to current 4D plugin development
68K-based Macintosh support (explicitly addressed by this note's platform-detection code) was phased out entirely as Apple and 4D moved to PowerPC-only and later Intel/Apple Silicon architectures

Modern 4D provides higher-level language commands (e.g. SELECTION TO ARRAY and related array/selection commands) for the kind of bulk field-to-array extraction that kEX_SUBSELECTION_TO_ARRAY provided at the plugin level
